rules.statement: Never write raw hex colors in markup or styles. Use the design system's color tokens.
rules.fix: Use a defined color token instead, e.g. var(--color-background), var(--color-foreground), var(--color-primary).

rules.statement: Never use Tailwind's built-in color palette utilities (bg-blue-500, text-red-600). Those colors are not part of this brand.
rules.fix: Use a semantic token utility bound to the design system (e.g. bg-primary, text-muted-foreground).

rules.statement: Never use Tailwind arbitrary-value brackets for spacing, sizing or color (p-[17px], w-[342px], bg-[#fff]). Every value must come from the scale.
rules.fix: Pick the nearest step on the defined spacing/sizing scale instead.

rules.statement: Never override border-radius inline. Radius is a system-level decision.
rules.fix: Use the radius tokens: var(--radius-sm), var(--radius-md), var(--radius-lg).

rules.statement: Use the project's existing components instead of writing raw HTML elements for anything the system already covers. Call get_component_contract before rendering a component to confirm its valid props.
rules.fix: Available components include: Button, Card, CardHeader, CardFooter.

rules.statement: Never pass a variant or size value that isn't declared in the component's contract. If the value you want doesn't exist, stop and ask rather than inventing one.
Never apply layout or color utility classes directly to a UI primitive to change its appearance. Extend the component's variants instead.
rules.fix: If a new visual treatment is genuinely needed, add a variant to the component rather than overriding at the call site.

rules.statement: Never use hype words in UI copy: seamless, effortless, unlock, revolutionize, supercharge, delight, magic, game-changing.
rules.fix: State plainly what the thing does.

rules.statement: Every empty state must end with a primary action the user can take. Never ship an empty state that only describes the absence of content.
